tools.name: hello
tools.description: Optional greeting. Greets you, remembers you if you pass your visitor token, and asks what you need. Use when you want this service to remember you across calls. Example arguments: {"name": "travel-planner-agent"}

tools.name: chat
tools.description: Talk in plain English (replies are in English): describe a task, say 'details 1', 'more', 'what's new', 'stop'. Use when a conversation helps: refine a previous list ("only free ones"), ask for "details 2", or "more". Example arguments: {"message": "find a weather forecast API"}

tools.name: search
tools.description: Read-only catalog lookup without saving a conversation. Return up to three relevant agents ranked by latest successful verification, recent activity, and quality grade. Searches A2A first, then MCP; x402 requires an explicit choice. Use when you need up to three ranked candidates for one task withou

tools.name: find_agents
tools.description: Read-only catalog lookup without saving a conversation. Return up to three active agents for a task, with verification evidence and calling details. Use when you need candidates plus verification evidence and connection steps for one task. Example arguments: {"task": "extract text from a PDF", "kind

tools.name: whats_new
tools.description: Read the last task saved by chat and re-evaluate its evidence without changing it. Use chat to save a task first (valid visitor token required). Use when you saved a task through chat earlier and want its evidence re-checked. Example arguments: {"visitor_token": "vt_..."}

tools.name: subscribe
tools.description: Legacy contact command. Use /api/task-updates with explicit task scope and authorization; this command cannot grant permission. Use only for legacy contact registration; task updates use /api/task-updates. Example arguments: {"contact_url": "https://example.org/hook", "contact_type": "webhook"}

tools.name: verify_contact
tools.description: Confirm your contact with the 6-digit code I sent there. Use after subscribe, with the code delivered to that contact. Example arguments: {"code": "123456", "visitor_token": "vt_..."}

tools.name: call
tools.description: Execute an admitted tool through the runtime gateway after checking its current schema and authorization. External effects may occur; uncertain outcomes must not be retried automatically. Use when you have chosen a listing and want this gateway to run one of its admitted tools. Example arguments: {"

tools.name: report
tools.description: Record caller feedback. On failure, suggest up to three currently verified alternatives and eligible published workflows without executing a retry. Retain the selected protocol and reject known shared failure domains. Use after a call to record the outcome and, on failure, get verified alternatives.

tools.name: credit
tools.description: Check your own virtual credit balance using a valid visitor token. Top-ups and subscriptions are being prepared; this tool only reads the current balance. Use when you need your own credit balance before a paid call. Example arguments: {"action": "balance", "visitor_token": "vt_..."}

tools.name: adapt_rest
tools.description: Universal Adapter: dynamically convert any OpenAPI/Swagger REST API specification into MCP tools and execute them. Use when the API you need has an OpenAPI document but no MCP server. Example arguments: {"spec_url": "https://api.example.org/openapi.json", "action": "list_tools"}

tools.name: search_workflows
tools.description: Find up to three relevant published workflows by purpose, node capability, or English and common non-English aliases. Discovery does not execute it. Use when a multi-step published workflow may already do your task. Example arguments: {"task": "technology news with supporting research"}

tools.name: workflow_details
tools.description: Read a currently public workflow definition and its recorded execution readiness. Review inputs and use the existing authorized workflow run API to execute. Use after search_workflows to inspect one workflow's steps and readiness. Example arguments: {"template_id": 12}

tools.name: run_workflow
tools.description: Run one published workflow after reviewing it with workflow_details. Pass the definition_hash you reviewed; a changed workflow is refused. Ask for a task (params.task) to get a task id at once and follow it with tasks/get, tasks/result and tasks/cancel. Only published templates run; paid (x402) step

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "subscribe" references sensitive artifacts (authorization). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: chat, whats_new, workflow_details · Private data: hello, search, whats_new, subscribe, verify_contact, report, credit, adapt_rest · Public sink: subscribe · Destructive: call, adapt_rest, search_workflows, workflow_details, run_workflow.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: chat, whats_new, workflow_details · Private data: hello, search, whats_new, subscribe, verify_contact, report, credit, adapt_rest · Public sink: subscribe · Destructive: call, adapt_rest, search_workflows, workflow_details, run_workflow

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
